stem: To estimate the effect of a discount email on spend, an analyst compares customers who got the email with those who did not, controlling for the number of site visits in the week after the email. Why is this a problem?

options.text: The email drives some of those visits, so this hides part of its effect
Site visits are a confounder here, so they must always be controlled for
Controlling for any extra variable always removes all bias
Site visits are a count, and counts cannot be used as controls
